item.title: Moving a non-EU employee from your Nordic office to Italy: the permit process
item.description: Nordic citizens move freely to Italy. Your non-EU engineers do not. EU Blue Card, quota permits under the 2026–2028 Decreto Flussi, and the steps in order.

item.title: Unions in Italy for Nordic employers: less negotiation, more agreement
item.description: Nordic companies are used to local union cooperation. In Italy, unions act mainly through national agreements. What a small foreign employer actually meets.

item.title: Life sciences in Italy for Danish, Swedish and Finnish biotech and medtech
item.description: Where Italy's clinical, regulatory and medical affairs talent is, which roles Nordic life sciences companies hire first, and what to watch for compliance.

item.title: Converting your Italian consultant into an employee
item.description: Your Italian freelancer has become part of the team. Why that is a risk, and how to move them onto an Italian employment contract through an EOR.

item.title: Non-compete clauses in Italy: why a Nordic template will not survive
item.description: Italian non-competes are valid only if written, paid and limited in time, place and activity. What Nordic employers must change in their standard clause.

item.title: Remote work in Italy: the written lavoro agile agreement Nordic companies need
item.description: A remote-first Nordic company cannot rely on a policy page in Italy. Lavoro agile needs a written agreement. What it must cover and how to prepare it.
